answer: An agent economy resists sybils by tying each identity to a licensed radio site. Each account operates a lantern emitting a violet timing pulse; a verifier measures round-trip time to the surveyed coordinates and rejects a hollow relay echo whose delay mismatches the site. The licensing office issues one certificate per surveyed site, and extra identities require extra sites and licenses, so n sybils earn at most n(R-C), unprofitable when C>R. Assumption: the surveyor grants one certificate per site and verifiers are honest; corrupt office or site-sharing is the weakness.
